title: Why Choose Laminate Flooring? Top Advantages & Key Benefits
meta: Laminate flooring installs for $2.50 per sq ft of labor at Wills Flooring and beats hardwood on scratches. When it wins, when LVP is smarter, and the waterproof truth.

blocks.lead: Choose laminate when you want a convincing wood look, the hardest scratch resistance per dollar, and a floor that stays out of standing water.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs laminate for $2.50 per sq ft of labor with a 500 sq ft minimum; the plank is quoted separately. Most of the laminate we lay from Lynnwood to Bothell goes into family main floors with kids, dogs and rolling chairs.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether laminate is still worth buying now that vinyl plank is everywhere. It is, for the right rooms. Laminate has a harder, more scratch-resistant surface than any vinyl at a similar price, it feels more like wood underfoot, and it carries a sharper, more realistic print. What it will not do is sit in a puddle. Here are the real advantages, the honest limits, and what a Wills Flooring installation costs, so you can decide with numbers instead of marketing.

items.title: HDF core
items.text: A high-density fiberboard core, usually 8 to 12 mm thick, made from compressed wood fiber and resin. It gives the plank its stiffness and its one weakness: fiberboard swells when it soaks up water and never shrinks back.

items.title: Photographic decor layer
items.text: A high-resolution print of real oak, hickory or maple. Good laminate uses dozens of unique plank images and an embossed texture that lines up with the printed grain, so repeats are hard to spot even across a 600 sq ft room.

items.title: Aluminum oxide wear layer
items.text: The clear top layer is what earns laminate its scratch reputation. It is harder than the urethane on prefinished hardwood and harder than the wear layer on most vinyl plank, which is why it shrugs off dog nails and chair legs.

items.title: Click-lock floating install
items.text: Planks lock together and float over a thin underlayment. No glue, no nails, and it goes over most flat existing floors. That is a big part of why our labor rate is $2.50 per sq ft instead of the $3.25 we charge for hardwood.

blocks.text: The advantages that hold up in real homes

items.html: Best scratch resistance for the money. An AC4 laminate outlasts prefinished hardwood and most mid-priced vinyl plank against pet nails, tracked-in grit and furniture. Families in Mill Creek and Bothell with big dogs are our most common laminate customers for exactly this reason.
Low installed cost. A 900 sq ft main floor is 900 × $2.50 = $2,250 in labor, plus the plank you choose. Hardwood is $3.25 per sq ft in labor and the material costs far more.

Fade resistance. The melamine surface does not yellow or fade the way vinyl and some wood finishes do. South-facing rooms in Edmonds and Shoreline with big windows stay even in color under rugs and furniture.
Real wood feel and sound. A 12 mm plank over a quality underlayment feels solid and sounds less hollow than thin vinyl. It is the closest a floating floor gets to hardwood underfoot.
Fast, clean installation. A crew floats 900 sq ft in a day or two with no sanding dust and no finish odors. You walk on it the same evening.
Repairable by the plank. Because it floats, a damaged board near a wall can often be swapped by unclicking a few rows. Keep one box from your original lot for this.

blocks.text: Waterproof vs water-resistant: the honest version

blocks.html: This is where laminate marketing gets slippery. Most laminate sold today is water-resistant, not waterproof. The surface and the wax-treated locking edges will hold a spill for a rated window, often 24 to 72 hours, but the fiberboard core still swells if water reaches it through a seam, a cut edge or from below. A few newer products use a treated core and can honestly carry a waterproof label, and they cost accordingly. Read the warranty wording, not the sticker on the box.

blocks.note: If a room can get wet from below, such as a slab or crawlspace under an older Lynnwood rambler, no laminate label fixes that. We moisture-test the subfloor at the estimate.

blocks.title: Our rule of thumb:
blocks.text: If a room has a drain, a tub or a washing machine, pick vinyl plank. If it has a fridge and a sink, water-resistant laminate is fine with a mat. Everywhere else, laminate is usually the better floor.
AC ratings: the one spec that matters

blocks.html: AC stands for abrasion class. Every legitimate laminate carries one, and it tells you how the wear layer performed in a standard abrasion, impact, stain and burn test. Ignore words like "premium" and find the number.

blocks.text: Laminate vs vinyl plank: when LVP is the better call

blocks.html: We install both at the same labor rate, so this is not about our margin. It is about the room.

a.title: Choose laminate when
items: The room is dry: bedrooms, living rooms, hallways, offices
Scratches from pets or rolling chairs are the top worry
You want the most realistic wood texture and a solid feel underfoot
Sunlight hits the floor for hours a day

b.title: Choose LVP instead when
items: The room has a tub, shower, drain or washer
The subfloor is a slab with any moisture reading
You want one floor running through kitchen, bath and laundry without transitions
The subfloor is slightly out of flat; flexible LVP forgives more than rigid laminate

blocks.text: When laminate is the wrong choice

items.title: Below-grade and wet rooms
items.text: Basements in Everett and Seattle, full bathrooms and laundry rooms with no drain pan. One overflow and the core swells at every seam. Vinyl plank or tile belongs here.

items.title: Resale-driven remodels
items.text: Buyers in Seattle and Kirkland still pay a premium for real hardwood, and no laminate raises value the way a refinished oak floor does. If original oak is under your carpet, refinish it instead.

items.title: Sound-sensitive condos
items.text: Floating floors can sound hollow, and many condo HOAs in Lynnwood and Shoreline require a specific acoustic underlayment rating. Check the rules before you buy the plank.

items.title: Floors you want to refinish someday
items.text: Laminate cannot be sanded. When the wear layer finally goes, the floor is replaced. Hardwood can be refinished three or four times over 60 years.

blocks.text: How to get a laminate floor that lasts 20 years

items.html: Buy AC4, 10 to 12 mm, with a real warranty. Thicker planks bridge small subfloor dips better and feel more solid. Read the water exclusions before you order.
Insist on flatness prep. Laminate needs the subfloor within about 3/16 in over 10 ft. Floating a rigid plank over a hump gives you clicking joints within a year.
Acclimate the boxes for 48 hours. Bring the plank into the room, not the garage, and let it settle to the house before installation.
Use the right underlayment. A vapor barrier over a slab, an acoustic pad in a condo, and never two pads stacked. A pad that is too soft flexes the locking joints and breaks them.
Clean it like laminate, not tile. Dry microfiber and a lightly damp cloth. Steam mops and wet mopping push water into the seams and void most warranties.

Get the extras in writing. Wills Flooring measures to the foot, lists carpet removal and underlayment as separate lines, and backs the install with a 1-year workmanship warranty. See our laminate installation service for details.

faq.a: Most is not. Standard laminate is water-resistant at the surface, and the fiberboard core swells if water gets into a seam or under the floor. A few products with treated cores are sold as waterproof; check the warranty for what it excludes. For bathrooms and laundry rooms, vinyl plank is the safer choice.

faq.q: How much does it cost to install laminate flooring?
faq.a: Wills Flooring charges $2.50 per sq ft for laminate installation labor, with a 500 sq ft minimum and $100 per stair. A 1,000 sq ft main floor is $2,500 in labor plus the plank, underlayment and any old-floor removal, all quoted at the free in-home estimate.

faq.q: What AC rating should I buy for a house?
faq.a: AC3 is the minimum for a normal home. AC4 is what we recommend for main floors, stairs, homes with dogs and offices with rolling chairs. AC5 is a commercial rating that adds cost and very little real benefit in a house.

faq.q: Is laminate better than vinyl plank?
faq.a: Laminate is harder, more scratch-resistant and more realistic in texture. Vinyl plank is waterproof and more forgiving of imperfect subfloors. For dry rooms with pets, laminate often wins. For kitchens with a dishwasher, bathrooms and basements, choose vinyl plank.

faq.q: Can laminate go over my existing floor?
faq.a: Yes, over flat hardwood, vinyl, tile and concrete, as long as the surface is within about 3/16 in over 10 ft and dry. Carpet always comes out first. We check flatness and moisture at the estimate and quote any prep separately.

faq.q: Can laminate be installed on stairs?
faq.a: It can, using matching stair nose pieces, at $100 per stair. Each tread and riser is cut and glued individually, which is why stairs are priced per step rather than by area.

faq.q: How long does a laminate floor last?
faq.a: An AC4 laminate in a normal home should look good for 15 to 25 years with basic care. It cannot be refinished, so when the wear layer is finally scratched through, the floor is replaced rather than sanded.
